title: Gmail for paralegals on Mac: email, templates and shortcuts for legal work with Lazur
metaTitle: Gmail for Paralegals on Mac: Shortcuts, Templates and Lazur Help
description: Gmail for paralegals on Mac: turn on shortcuts, save templates, triage client mail, and ask Lazur to walk you through each step in your browser.
intro: Gmail for paralegals on Mac means running Gmail in Safari or Chrome for client, witness and court correspondence. Turn on keyboard shortcuts, save the emails you write every week as templates, and label threads by matter so nothing gets lost. Lazur can read the screen and guide you through each step, but every step on this page works without it.
tldr: Turn on keyboard shortcuts first: Settings > See all settings > Settings, then Save Changes.
Save repeat emails as templates under More options > Templates. Google says templates work on a computer only.
Label threads by matter and archive them when they close, so you can find them later.
Lazur points, guides and drafts text. It does not click or send for you.

blocks.text: Most paralegals on a Mac open Gmail in a browser tab, usually Safari or Chrome, and keep it open all day. Gmail works the same way in either browser. What changes is how fast you move through it. This page covers the Gmail features that matter for paralegal work, how to turn each one on, and where Lazur fits in.
What paralegals use email for on a Mac

The U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics lists the core paralegal duties. They include drafting correspondence and legal documents, such as confirmation letters and contracts. They include calling clients, witnesses and lawyers to set up interviews, meetings and depositions. They also include sending exhibits, briefs and other documents to courts, agencies or opposing counsel.
The BLS page never mentions email. So the email part of this page is our inference from those duties, not a finding from BLS. In most offices, though, much of that work starts or ends in an inbox.

About 404,900 paralegals and legal assistants were employed in 2025. Their median pay in May 2025 was $62,890 a year, or $30.24 an hour. Those figures show how big the job is. They do not show how the day splits between email and everything else.
Turn on Gmail keyboard shortcuts before you need them

Gmail keyboard shortcuts are off until you turn them on. Many people never find the setting. Action and navigation shortcuts do nothing until it is on. Open Settings > See all settings, then choose the Settings tab. Turn on keyboard shortcuts, then select Save Changes. Click into your inbox and press / to test it. The search box should open.
The Gmail keyboard shortcuts that matter for legal mail

items: / opens search. Use it to find a client name, a case number or a witness.
r replies to the open message.
e archives the conversation. Use it when a thread is finished, not while a reply is pending.
n and p move to the next and previous message in an open conversation.
⌘ + ; jumps to the next misspelled word. Google marks this one as Mac-only.
⌘ Enter sends the message from the compose window.

blocks.text: Google's full list is on its Keyboard shortcuts for Gmail page, linked in the sources below. Do not try to learn all of them. Pick the three or four you will use every day, and let the rest wait.

blocks.title: Spell check misses names
blocks.text: ⌘ + ; steps you through misspelled words, but a spell checker does not know your client's surname. Check party names, case numbers and dates by eye before you press ⌘ Enter.
Set up Gmail templates for repeat legal emails

Paralegals send the same messages again and again. Document requests, scheduling notes and status updates look nearly the same each time. A template turns that text into one insert. Templates are a Gmail feature you must turn on first. Google says templates can only be turned on and used from Gmail on a computer, so do this in Safari or Chrome on your Mac.

items: Open Settings > See all settings, then choose the Advanced tab.
Next to Templates, click Enable.
Select Save Changes.
Compose a new message and write the text you reuse.
Click More options > Templates > Save draft as template, then choose Save as new template.

blocks.text: Name each template after the task, not the case. Deposition time request still works next month. A name tied to one matter does not, because you will reuse the text on other matters. Put the variable parts in square brackets, such as [date] and [witness name]. Fill them in after you insert the template. A bracket you forget to fill in is easy to spot before it goes out.
Insert and delete Gmail templates

To use a template, click Compose, then choose More options > Templates > Insert template. Pick the template from the list. The text drops into the message body. Check the To line, the subject and every date before you press ⌘ Enter. A template fixes the text, not the recipient or the dates.

To delete a template, go to More options > Templates > Delete template. Google says a deleted template cannot be recovered. Before you delete one, copy its text into a note. That takes a moment and saves a rewrite later.
How to edit a Gmail template with no edit button

Gmail has no edit button for templates. Almost everyone hunts for one at first. To change a template, write the new version in a compose window. Then choose More options > Templates > Save draft as template. Under Overwrite Template, pick the template you want to replace, then click Save.

Here is a real case. Your status update template says the discovery window is open. It has closed. Open a new message, type the corrected text, and overwrite the old template. Then insert it into a blank draft to check the result. Copy the old wording first if you may need it again, because the overwrite replaces it.
Template mistakes that cost paralegals time

items: Saving a template with a client's name in it. Strip names out before you save, or the next insert may carry one client's details to another matter.
Overwriting the wrong template. Read the names in the list before you click Save, because one wrong click replaces a template you still use.
Planning a mobile send around a template. Google limits templates to a computer, so write from your Mac when you need one.
Building a template for every case. Keep a short set of general templates and fill in the details each time.
Assuming there is a cap. Google's template page does not state a limit on how many templates you can save, so you have no number to plan around.

blocks.text: Where admin time goes in legal work

Admin work takes time from billable work across the legal field. An 8am survey of 400 legal professionals, including attorneys, paralegals and legal operations staff, found that nearly 40% estimate losing four or more billable hours a week to admin tasks. The survey does not report paralegals on their own. Read that figure as a general signal, not a paralegal number.

Time tracking came out as the biggest admin stressor, named by 44% of respondents. Two-thirds said admin work sometimes gets in the way of their core responsibilities. The survey does not split out email. Email is still one place admin work arrives, so the same habits apply: short templates, clear labels and fewer open threads.

Gmail labels, filters and snooze for busy inboxes

Label each thread by matter, then archive it when the matter closes. A label keeps a case together without a folder tree. Follow the [label guide](/how-to/create-a-label-in-gmail) to create one. Then use the [filter guide](/how-to/create-a-filter-in-gmail) to send mail from a court or a regular client straight into its label. Check the filter's results after a day, so you know it catches the right mail. Older threads still need a label by hand. The [archive guide](/how-to/archive-emails-in-gmail) covers the steps for clearing finished matters.

Snooze hides a thread until a time you pick. Use it for the thread that needs a reply on Friday, not the one you already answered. The [snooze guide](/how-to/snooze-an-email-in-gmail) shows the steps in Safari and Chrome. Shared inboxes get messy fast. A 2024 survey of in-house legal teams by Dilitrust found 31% spend at least 8 hours a week on internal email questions, and many of those questions repeat. Paralegals are not a separate group in that survey, so read it as a pattern, not a paralegal number.
Avoid CC and BCC mistakes in legal email

Copying the wrong person causes real trouble in legal mail. A BCC line hides recipients from each other, which matters when you send one client update to several parties. The [CC and BCC guide](/how-to/add-cc-and-bcc-in-gmail) shows where those fields sit in Gmail and which shortcuts open them. Check both lines every time you reply all.

Long threads with many copied people fill the inbox fast. Mute a conversation you only need to watch, using the [mute guide](/how-to/mute-a-conversation-in-gmail). If the inbox still feels crowded, change the display density so more threads fit on screen. The [display density guide](/how-to/change-display-density-in-gmail) has the menu paths.
Schedule calls, interviews and depositions by email

The BLS says paralegals call clients, witnesses and lawyers to set up interviews, meetings and depositions. A lot of that starts as an email. Put the date options, the location and the dial-in details in the first message. A clear first email cuts the back and forth, and it gives the other side less to misread.

Send later helps when the other side works in another time zone. Write the message now and schedule it for the start of their day. The [schedule guide](/how-to/schedule-an-email-to-send-later-in-gmail) shows the steps for Safari and Chrome. After you schedule it, read the send time once more before you close the window. For your own follow-ups, ask Lazur to add an Apple Reminders item for the day you need to check.
Where Lazur fits in the same Gmail session

Lazur is a voice assistant for the Mac that lives in the notch. Hold ⌥ ⌘, which means Option and Command together, and ask about anything on screen. Lazur answers out loud. Use it on a long thread when you need one date or one name fast, without scrolling through the whole thread.

Ask where a button is, and Lazur draws a circle and a label around it. Ask how to do something, and it guides you one click at a time, waiting for each click. It does not click for you. You stay in charge of every send, archive and delete.

Hold fn to dictate clean text at the cursor in any app, including a Gmail compose window. Lazur also keeps snippets, a personal dictionary and clipboard slots. Add the spelling of a witness's surname to the dictionary, so dictation gets it right. Research requests run in Lazur's own Chrome tabs and come back with a summary and a report. That helps when you need public court rules pulled together.
What Lazur sees, and what your firm may not allow

Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers so they can answer you. They are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models. Lazur also keeps a memory of what you asked and did, and that memory stays on your Mac.

Client email can be confidential, and your firm may have rules about AI tools. Read that policy before you hold the shortcut over a privileged thread. Lazur's privacy terms do not replace your firm's rules. If the policy bars sending client content to outside services, leave Lazur closed on those threads and work in Gmail alone.
A worked example: confirming a deposition by email

items: Open the thread with the deposition notice. Press / and type the witness name if the thread is buried.
Hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask Lazur which date and time the notice gives. Lazur answers out loud.
Click Compose, then choose More options > Templates > Insert template and pick your confirmation template.
Hold fn and dictate the changed details. Read the names and the time by eye.
Check the To line, then press ⌘ Enter to send.
Press e to archive the thread after the witness confirms.

blocks.text: You make every click in that example. Lazur points, reads and types. The send and the archive are your decisions, which is how it should work for legal mail.
Mistakes to avoid when you use Gmail with Lazur

items: Holding the shortcut over a thread your firm bars from outside services.
Expecting Lazur to press Send. It drafts and types text. You press ⌘ Enter or click Send.
Dictating case numbers and dates without a read back. Dictation is fast, but the result still needs your eyes.
Skipping the keyboard shortcuts setting, then blaming Gmail. The shortcuts do nothing until you turn them on.

blocks.title: Mac only, for now
blocks.text: Lazur runs on macOS, on Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Windows is planned, not available. Gmail itself runs in your browser, so every Gmail step on this page works in Safari or Chrome.
What to do next

Start with the keyboard shortcuts setting, then save the two templates you write most often. If you want Lazur in the same session, [download Lazur](/download) for your Mac and start the free trial. You do not need a credit card to start. Plans are on the [pricing page](/pricing).

faq.question: Is there a Gmail app for Mac?
faq.answer: Gmail on a Mac runs in your browser. This page uses Safari and Chrome. We did not verify a separate Gmail desktop app, so every step here assumes the browser version.

faq.question: Why do my Gmail keyboard shortcuts not work?
faq.answer: Keyboard shortcuts must be turned on. Go to Settings > See all settings > Settings, turn on keyboard shortcuts, then select Save Changes. Action and navigation shortcuts stay off until you do.

faq.question: Can I use Gmail templates on my iPhone?
faq.answer: No, not for setup or use. Google says templates can only be turned on and used from Gmail on a computer. Do template work in Safari or Chrome on your Mac.

faq.question: Is there a limit on how many Gmail templates I can save?
faq.answer: Google's template help page does not state a limit. Some third-party guides mention caps, but Google's page names no number, so do not plan around one.

faq.question: Can Lazur send the email for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur drafts and types text, and it guides you one click at a time. It does not click buttons. You press ⌘ Enter or click Send yourself.

faq.question: Does Lazur watch my whole screen all the time?
faq.answer: No. Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer you, and they are not stored.

faq.question: Can I recall an email after I send it?
faq.answer: Our recall guide covers what Gmail allows and the Undo Send steps. Read it before you rely on recall for a message that already went to a court or opposing counsel.

faq.question: Does Lazur run on Windows?
faq.answer: Not yet. Lazur runs on macOS, on Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Windows is planned, not available.

faq.question: Do I need Lazur to follow this guide?
faq.answer: No. Every Gmail step on this page works without Lazur. Lazur helps when you want the steps read aloud or pointed out on screen.
